companion: dsh-plugin-resolution.json records what shipping a host-side provider costs
conclusion: No configuration of an MCP entry can bind identity on this host: the transport discards the session, and the child environment carries only what the (copyable) entry configures. Closing the counterexample therefore needs a tool provider that runs INSIDE the harness process and reads the live session per call, i.e. a DSH plugin using ctx.tools.register + exec.agent.session, in place of @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client. Until such a provider exists and the bridge requires the identity it supplies, the overlay carries a credential and not a proof of the caller, and the executor does not claim R1 closed. The companion finding dsh-plugin-resolution.json shows such a provider must be a package installed into the profile-local prefix, which makes closing R1 a product change rather than a configuration fix.

counter_evidence_same_build.meaning: inside the harness process a tool implementation CAN read the live session; only the MCP transport loses it

observations.child_environment: function buildChildEnv(extra) { return { ...scrubbedParentEnv(), ...extra }; } and the stdio transport passes env: buildChildEnv(config.env) — so a child sees the scrubbed parent environment plus exactly what the entry configures
observations.initialize_client_info: no clientInfo construction in this package; the handshake is performed by @modelcontextprotocol/client, which has no conversation to name
